Because the emptiness of the essence of non-existence is itself non-existent, the <term>Bodhisattva</term> <gloss>one who seeks awakening for the sake of all beings</gloss> is not perceived at the final limit. Because the emptiness of the essence of non-existence is empty, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the final limit. Because the emptiness of the essence of non-existence is secluded <note>original: "dben pa", meaning isolated or void of inherent nature</note>, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the final limit. Because the emptiness of the essence of non-existence is non-existent, and because the emptiness of the essence of existence is without essence, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the final limit.

Because the emptiness of the essence of non-existence is non-existent, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. Because the emptiness of the essence of non-existence is empty, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. Because the emptiness of the essence of non-existence is secluded, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. The Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. The Bodhisattva is perceived as the three <note>likely referring to the three times: past, present, and future</note>. The Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. Because the emptiness of the essence of non-existence is empty, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle.

Why is that so? O venerable <term>Sharadvatiputra</term> <gloss>Shariputra, one of the primary disciples of the Buddha</gloss>, in the non-existence of the emptiness of the essence of non-existence, in the emptiness of the emptiness of the essence of non-existence, in the seclusion of the emptiness of the essence of non-existence, and in the lack of essence of the emptiness of the essence of non-existence, the prior limit is not perceived.

<summary>This page discusses the philosophical concept of emptiness regarding the nature of a Bodhisattva. It argues that because the essence of non-existence is itself empty and non-existent, a Bodhisattva cannot be found or perceived at the beginning, middle, or end of time.</summary>
